 06 Nov 2026 Arteta expecting stern test from "impressive" Hull
 Connor Booth 0
 0
 0
 0
 0
 0
 Mikel Arteta has been impressed with what he's seen from newly-promoted Hull City both in their promotion campaign and their start to the Premier League season.  
 Despite being winless in their last eight games in all competitions, the Tigers have been picking up points with five draws in their opening nine games back in the big time, losing just twice in the league this season. 
 We'll be hoping to inflict a third defeat on Sergej Jakirovic's side when he host Hull at Emirates Stadium on Saturday afternoon. 
 "It's been an incredibly journey from what the club has done last year." the boss said on the Tigers. 
 "Some of the difficult games they've come through and competed in, they've earned the right to be here and been impressive. 
 "We've been discussing that with the boys on what to expect from them tomorrow and to be clear on what we need to do to beat them. Tomorrow is the main focus of everything we've done, we need to go, be better than Hull, and beat them." 
 Every word of Mikel Arteta's pre-Hull City presser Read more Tomorrow's game will be the last for both clubs before the November international break, after which we'll be taking on Newcastle United away from home. 
 But having spent much of the early part of the 2026/27 season travelling, we'll then have 11 consecutive games in London upon our return from Tyneside, including seven at Emirates Stadium. 
 The boss has been impressed with how we've coped with our demanding schedule so far, with just one 90-minute defeat in all competitions this season. 
 "We have to navigate with [the schedule] and have done it really well so far, with a lot of difficult opponents and travel. We want to attack again tomorrow, right from the off. 
 "We know the momentum, especially going into the international break because we know what's coming after November and December." 
 Five Gunners called up to England squad Read more While our attacking football has been beautiful to watch at times this season, we've maintained the defensive superiority that saw us win the Premier League title last season. 
 Mikel feels that our levels all over the pitch, both in an attacking and defensive sense, need to continue to hit the high standards we demand of ourselves if we are to be champions again. 
 "It does matter, everything matters. You are able to [win] because of the compromise and commitment of every single player. 
 "The same with attack responsibility, anything related to set-pieces, transitions, everything as a whole. 
 "You need to sustain an incredible level across 10 months and to do that, you need to have everything. Otherwise, you won't be able to do it."
